text: ABSTRACT
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > ABSTRACT

text: Polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) is studied in this paper as an inhibitor of cobalt electrodeposition. The suppres sion effect of PVP was analyzed through electrochemical methods, including cyclic voltammetry (CV) and galvanostatic measurements (GM) tests. It is indicated that PVP effectively suppresses the electrodeposition of cobalt and chloride ion accelerates this suppression. Further experiments verify that PVP inhibits the deposition of cobalt through the adsorption on the electrode surface. Quantum chemical calculations were employed to calculate the molecular orbitals of PVP and the electrostatic potential (ESP) energy of the involved molecules. The simulation results imply that the amide group acts as the main electrophilic attack region and facilitates nucleophilic reactions to bond with cobalt. High aspect ratio trench filling on silicon wafer was achieved with the addition of PVP, which confirms that PVP is an applicable inhibitor for the practical electrodeposition of cobalt filling. The mechanism of cobalt trench filling was proposed to explain the role of PVP in the electroplating filling.

text: 1. Introduction
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 1. Introduction

text: Metals are the basic building materials to establish the conductive interconnection between the electronic components. The inherent properties of the metal are critical factors for achieving high density interconnection and miniaturization in the electronic devices. Compared with copper, cobalt with shorter electron Mean Free Path (MFP) holds the reduced resistance scaling effect and has been considered as a favorable interconnect metal [1 3]. Also, the thermal expansion coefficient (CTE) of cobalt is close to the one of silicon, which enables cobalt to serve as a compatible metal integrated in silicon-based electronic chips. In comparison with aluminum and copper, cobalt is recommended to be one of the next generation interconnection metals by the leading semiconductor manufacturers, such as Intel and Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE), to meet the requirement of the blooming 5 G communication. Generally, inter-layer connections within the silicon chips are electroplated by bottom-up super filling of through-holes, microvias and trenches.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 1. Introduction

text: Cobalt alloys have been playing an important role in aviation components, medical devices and other fields due to its high mechanical strength and wear resistance [4 6]. The researches on pure cobalt electro-depositing are still insufficient because the electrodeposition of cobalt suffers from the intrinsic hydrogen evolution, poor throwing power (deposition uniformity, TP) and inferior plating quality of the deposited cobalt layer [7].
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 1. Introduction

text: Additives are usually involved in electrolyte to promote plating properties. Researchers have performed extensive experimental as well as theoretical analysis to investigate the growth mechanism and additive behaviors of bottom-up copper super filling for micro-vias [8 11]. It was found that, the additives with the function of increasing metal deposition overpotential are able to obtain void-free super-filling [12]. Convection-dependent adsorption (CDA) of additive causes larger differential current distribution to realize higher deposition rate at the bottom than the one at the surface of microvia [13]. However, researches focusing on the additives involved in cobalt electrodepositing are still inadequate, especially in cobalt super filling.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 1. Introduction

text: Huang et al. found that dimethylglyoxime (DMG) exhibits obvious suppression behavior in cobalt electro-deposition [14,15]. They stated that paired amine groups of DMG enable the strong complexing between DMG molecule and cobalt ion. On the other hand, these groups also contribute to the preferred absorption of DMG on the deposited cobalt surface. DMG is, however, not an appropriate candidate for industrial application because the molecular chain of DMG easily breaks down under electric current. In addition, the low solubility in acidic aqueous solution also hinders the feasibility of DMG. PVP is a neutral non-ionic polymer containing paired amine groups with good complexing ability [16 18]. Notably, PVP is soluble in water and most organic solvents with low toxicity, making PVP a potential additive for cobalt super-filling.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 1. Introduction

text: In this paper, PVP was studied as major additive for cobalt super filling by electro-plating. The suppression effect of PVP was investigated by electrochemical experiments and the effect of chloride ion was also studied. Moreover, the active site in PVP molecule was speculated by theoretical calculations to understand the mechanism of suppression. In addition, PVP also displays significant influence on the morphology and crystal phase of electrodeposited cobalt. As for practical application, trench super-filling was realized by electrodepositing with PVP.

section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3. Results and discussion

text: 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition

text: The inhibitive behavior of PVP in the solution was investigated through electrochemical measurements. Fig. 1 shows the significant decrease of cobalt stripping area and hysteretic voltammetric features in the solution with PVP. The current density decreases sharply in the presence of PVP (Fig. 1a). For example, after adding 5 mg/L PVP into plating solution, the stripping peak current density decreases from 2 1 mA/cm2 to 1 2 mA/cm2.. In the meantime, the oxidation peak potential is also shifted negatively by 80 mV (from 0.36 V to 0.44 V vs Hg/ Hg _2 SO _4). The change in stripping peak current density and oxidation peak potential both reveal that cobalt electrodeposition is inhibited by PVP. The CV plot in Fig. 1b highlights that the cobalt deposition potential is negative correlated with the concentration of PVP which shows an enhancing effect on the polarization of cobalt electroplating. In addition, with the increasing concentration of PVP, cobalt electrodepositing was further inhibited, which is supported by the decreasing area of oxidation peaks.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition
Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition

text: The maximum state of PVP suppression was further studied. As is shown in Fig. 1c, the oxidation peak area of CV was calculated to illustrate the inhibition effect of PVP with different concentrations. The integral of the cobalt stripping peak area is defined as Q_0 without PVP and as Q with PVP, respectively [28]. The curve which displays the value of Q/Q_0 as a function of the concentration of PVP can be divided into three stages (Fig. 1d). Q/Q_0 values undergo a sharp drop with low concentration of PVP and a steady stage with the high concentration of PVP. Notably, an intermediate slope appears in the curve for the PVP concentration range between 15 mg/L and 81 mg/L. When the PVP concentration continues to increase to more than 81 mg/L, the inhibition of PVP in cobalt electroplating reaches maximum.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition

text: As well known, chloride ions could affect the quality of metal coating and influence the mechanisms of additives in metal electroplating bath [29, 30]. The impact of Cl in the PVP-involved electroplating system was analyzed through voltammetry curves (Fig. 2a). In contrast with the curves in Fig. 1a-b, the stripping peak current density decreases more sharply when 5 mg/L PVP was added into the solution. These results in CV curve imply that PVP can inhibit the electrodeposi tion of cobalt in both chloride-containing and non-chloride ion plating solutions. However, in the solution with Cl, less amount of PVP is needed to reach the saturation (Fig. 2b). As for the Q/Q_0 value, this ratio decreases with increasing concentration of PVP and process is divided into two stages (Fig. 2b). The phenomenon of first stage that Q/Q_0 values decrease sharply with adding PVP can be observed when the concentration of PVP is less than 10.65 mg/L. In the second stage, Q/Q values maintain relatively stable with further increased PVP concentration. In the absence of Cl (Fig. 1d), PVP in plating solution reaches the saturation at a much higher concentration.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.1. Inhibition and maximum ofPVP inhibition

text: Furthermore, when 10 mg/L PVP was added, the oxidation peak area in solution with Cl (Q/Q_0 value decreases from 1.0 to 0.42 in Fig. 2b) decreased more than the chlorine-free solution (Q/Q_0 value decreases from 1.0 to 0.51 in Fig. 1d). It is indicated that PVP is a suppressant of electrodeposited cobalt which can negatively shifts the deposition potential of cobalt, and chloride ion helps to accelerate the suppression effect of PVP.

text: The increase of overpotential is attributed to the adsorption of PVP on the surface of cobalt. The reverse scan exhibits an obvious hysteresis in the solution with only 100 mg/L PVP (Fig. 2c), revealing an adsorption and re-adsorption process of PVP. After adding Cl into PVP solution, the CV curve in Fig. 2c displays a weaker hysteresis effect. Thus, the adsorption strength of PVP is enhanced and Cl makes the adsorption more stable. Fig. 2c also shows the synergistic effect between PVP molecules and chloride ions. Chlorine ions were added to the solution containing 100 mg/L PVP, and the absolute value of current density continued to decrease.

text: The interaction between PVP and cobalt cations in aqueous solution has been reported (Liu et al.) [17, 31]. In this work, when the PVP was added in the solution, it preferentially complexes with cobalt ion. PVP-CO ^2 + complexes affect the polarization of cobalt electrodeposition and thus inhibit cobalt deposition. As the concentration of PVP increases, an extra oxidation peak appears with stronger suppression. PVP molecules are absorbed on the electrode surface and chloride ions promote the adsorption of PVP.

text: 3.2. Quantum chemical calculation and CDA
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.2. Quantum chemical calculation and CDA
Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.2. Quantum chemical calculation and CDA

text: The molecular frontier orbital theory suggests that the key of chemical reactions is the HOMO and LUMO of the molecules [20]. The distribution of HOMO and LUMO of PVP was simulated by molecular orbital method (Fig. 3). The HOMO value ( E _ HOMO) of a molecule determines its ability to lose electrons outward, and the LUMO value ( E _ LUMO) represents its ability to accept electrons. Higher E and lower E _ LUMO partly reflect the reactivity of molecule [32]. The E _ HOMO value of PVP is 6.877 eV (Fig. 3e), compared with 7.338 eV of PEG [21], indicating that PVP has relatively stronger electron donating ability. The simulated values imply that PVP is more likely to interact with cobalt cations and have an impact on electrodeposition of cobalt. Fig. 3e shows that the nitrogen element and oxygen element of the amide group are the main contributors to the HOMO orbital, which acts as the main electrophilic attack region. The organics with higher value of E _ HOMO tent to have stronger electron donating ability to bond with the d-orbital of the metal. PVP with amide group may bond with cobalt, facilitates formation of PVP adsorption and inhibits cobalt electroplating.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.2. Quantum chemical calculation and CDA

text: The electrostatic potential distribution on the surface of molecular van der Waals force of PVP is displayed in Fig. 3a, which is widely used to predict molecular electron donating ability, electro-accepting ability and electrophilic reaction sites [33]. Areas with low ESP value are the positions of high electron density, which are considered to be more affinitive to the cobalt surface [34, 35]. PVP has lowest ESP value of 131.3 kJ/mol compared with PEG [21] ( 131.6 kJ/mol) (Fig. 3a). The electron density map shows that the carbonyl of the amide group contributes greatly to the electron donating ability of PVP. The amide group probably acts as reaction sites in the electrodeposition reaction by the quantum chemical calculations.

text: Convection have significant influence on the process of electrodeposition. For the electroplating with rotating electrodes, the higher rotating speed of electrode leads to the greater convection in the solution. PVP can effectively inhibit the electrodeposition of cobalt in strong convection because the potential was quickly reduced by 160 mV when 5 mg/L PVP was added in strong convection (2000 rpm) (Fig. 3c). However, when 5 mg/L of PVP was added at low rotating speed (200 rpm), the potential was reduced by 100 mV and the inhibitory effect was slowly balanced after 2000s. Ji et al. found that electrolyte flow plays an important role in electroplating process [36]. The convection intensity of the solution inside the hole is lower than the one outside. The local convection affects the transport boundary layer in cobalt electroplating. As a result, more PVP molecules are be transmitted from solution to the electrode surface per unit time in strong convection. In Fig. 3c, PVP demonstrates a faster suppression in the strong convective condition, which is conducive to filling holes in electroplating.

text: PVP molecules can be adsorbed on surface faster, resulting in different concentration distribution of additives at surface and bottom of trenches at the initial stage of electrodeposition. The cause of the secondary current density distribution is the concentration gradient of the additive [37,38]. In addition, the electroplating experiment was also conducted. As shown in Fig. 3d, the silicon trench is sealed in cobalt electroplating without inhibitor during the process of cobalt electroplating which is consistent with the above discussion.

text: 3.3. Cobalt trench electrodeposition
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.3. Cobalt trench electrodeposition

text: Cobalt filling was achieved in silicon trenches, which confirms that PVP is capable of being an inhibitor in the electrodeposited cobalt filling. The silicon-based chip has a series of trenches in which a layer of gold was sputtered and the recess was filled by electrodepositing cobalt (Fig. 4). Fig. 4d is a cross-sectional slice of the electrodeposited cobalt-filled silicon trench with full cobalt super-filling. In this work, cobalt super-filling is achieved in silicon trench with the addition of 100 mg/L PVP. It is assumed that PVP molecules adsorb rapidly on the plated surface in the presence of Cl.

caption: Fig. 5. the strategy for bottom up super-filling with three stages.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.3. Cobalt trench electrodeposition

text: Cobalt bottom up filling mechanism is proposed in Fig. 5. In the initial stage of electrodeposition, PVP molecules were quickly adsorbed on the surface, strongly inhibiting the growth of cobalt on the surface. Therefore, the deposition rate at the bottom is greater than that at the surface. Diffusional limitation and CDA of PVP long chain molecule both contribute to the higher deposition rate at the bottom than the one at the surface of the trench and obvious bottomup filling is then expected.

text: 3.4. Surface characterization
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.4. Surface characterization

text: The effect of PVP involved in the electrodeposition of cobalt was further investigated by the characterization of morphology. PVP demonstrates considerable effect on electrodeposited cobalt crystals. The XRD results in Fig. 6a indicate that PVP inhibits the cobalt electrodeposition by affecting the growth of cobalt specific crystal surfaces. The electrodeposited cobalt mainly forms cubic crystals in Fig. 6a. And, it is worth mentioning that PVP reduced the intensity of diffraction peak of cobalt along the direction of 220, indicating that the introduction of PVP inhibited the growth of 220 surface of cobalt without affecting the growth of other crystal planes.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.4. Surface characterization

text: The contact angle test indicates that PVP can improve the wettability of plating solution effectively. As is shown in Fig. 6c-d, the contact angle of the plating solution without PVP is more than 3 0 ^° on the cobalt surface and is reduced to 15° after adding 100 mg/L PVP. Better wettability of the solution enables more hydrogen to be released in time [39] and enhances coating quality in cobalt electrodeposition. PVP can also be used as surfactant in electrodeposited cobalt because the amide group and carbon chains of PVP can act as polar hydrophilic and hydrophobic group respectively. Meanwhile, according to the theory of electro-capillary, polarization can reduce the surface tension and contributes to the desorption of hydrogen, which is consistent with the discussion above.

text: In addition, PVP can refine particles and makes the cobalt layer more compact. The SEM images of electrodeposited cobalt in the solution without PVP display different particle size and roughness of surface without inhibitor (Fig. 6e). Fig. 6f shows the SEM of electrodeposited cobalt layer after adding 100 mg/L PVP and the surface morphology of the coating changed obviously in contrast with the one without PVP.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 3.4. Surface characterization

text: The uniformity of the coating was clearly improved by 3D roughness tests (Fig. 6g-h), and cobalt surface becomes more compact. Sa represents the arithmetic mean of the height values of all the peaks and troughs on plane A in Fig. 6g and Fig. 6h. The larger the value of Sa, the greater roughness of metal surface. The Sa value of electrodeposited cobalt layer in the solution without PVP is less than the Sa value of cobalt layer with 100 mg/L PVP in the electroplating solution, validating that PVP can improve the uniformity of cobalt layer in cobalt electrodeposition. In summary, PVP is an effective cobalt electrodeposition inhibitor. Besides, PVP can effectively facilitate hydrogen desorption, affect the surface morphology, and improve surface uniformity of cobalt layer.

text: 4. Conclusions
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 4. Conclusions

text: As a conclusion, PVP can increase the polarization of electrodeposition, affect the growth of cobalt particles growth and redistribute the cathodic current. PVP works as inhibitor for electrodeposited cobalt and the suppression mechanisms of PVP were demonstrated. Chloride ion can facilitate the adsorption of PVP and helps to accelerate the suppression effect of PVP. The amide group of PVP is probably the reaction site by quantum chemical calculations. Void free filling of silicon trenches was achieved by cobalt super-filling on a sputtered gold layer in this paper.
section: Investigation of polyvinylpyrrolidone as an inhibitor for trench super-filling of cobalt electrodeposition > 4. Conclusions

text: Cobalt electroplating has great application potential in the fabrication of interconnection in electronic devices. More types of additives with the function of manipulating cobalt deposition rate and improving deposition quality of cobalt layer will be attempted in the following research.
